title: Did you know… David encouraged himself when no one else did?
paragraphs: Did you know… David encouraged himself when no one else did?

He was abandoned.
Mocked.
Exhausted.
And then it got worse.

David came back to camp… and everything was gone.
Burned.
His family—taken.
Even his own men, the ones he fought beside, started whispering about killing him.

No support.
No comfort.
No one clapping for him.
Just silence… and pressure.
But then one line cuts through the darkness like fire:
“But David strengthened himself in the Lord his God.” — 1 Samuel 30:6

No worship team.
No pastor.
No friend to pray for him.
David preached to his own soul.

He reminded himself who God is.
Faithful.
Near.
Still King—even in chaos.
But here’s what we miss…

David didn’t just hype himself up.
He turned back to God.

That’s repentance.
That’s surrender.
That’s real strength.

Because the truth is—
sometimes God will allow isolation
so your dependence becomes real.

No crowd.
No noise.
Just you… and Him.
And in that place, something holy happens.

You stop leaning on people—
and start leaning on grace.
And that grace has a name:
Jesus.

The Son of David who didn’t just encourage Himself—
He carried the cross alone.

Rejected.
Beaten.
Forsaken.

So that when you feel abandoned,
you are never truly alone.

Because of Christ, your lowest moment
can become your turning point.

So if nobody’s calling you today…
if nobody’s checking in…
Preach to your soul.

God is still good.
God is still near.
God is still for you in Christ.
And this is not the end of your story.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
